claim: Quiescent yeast cells display numerous small vesicular mitochondria.
source: Indeed, while quiescent yeast cells display numerous small vesicular mitochondria, senescent cells exhibit few globular mitochondria.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the manuscript with microscopy data.

claim: Senescent yeast cells exhibit few globular mitochondria.
source: Indeed, while quiescent yeast cells display numerous small vesicular mitochondria, senescent cells exhibit few globular mitochondria.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the manuscript with microscopy data.

claim: Cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by replicative age.
source: We demonstrate that cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by replicative age, volume or density.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that mother cells with different numbers of bud scars have similar re-proliferation capacities.

claim: Cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by volume.
source: We demonstrate that cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by replicative age, volume or density.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that cells with vesicular mitochondria can re-proliferate regardless of their volume.

claim: Cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by density.
source: We demonstrate that cell's propensity to enter quiescence is not influenced by replicative age, volume or density.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using density gradient fractionation showing that cells with vesicular mitochondria from different density fractions have similar re-proliferation capacities.

claim: Quiescent cells' ability to survive is significantly improved when they exhibit specific reorganization of several cellular machineries.
source: Overall, our findings reveal that quiescent cells are not all identical but that their ability to survive is significantly improved when they exhibit the specific reorganization of several cellular machineries.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that cells with vesicular mitochondria, actin bodies, and proteasome storage granules have higher re-proliferation capacities.

claim: Upon glucose exhaustion, mitochondria tubules progressively fragment into numerous small cortical vesicles in cells entering quiescence.
source: We demonstrate that in cells entering quiescence, mitochondrial tubules progressively fragment into numerous small cortical vesicles.
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-course microscopy data showing the progression of mitochondrial morphology changes.

claim: Cells that will enter senescence display few large globular mitochondria that form upon the diauxic shift.
source: In contrast, cells that will enter senescence display few large globular mitochondria that form upon the diauxic shift.
evidence: This is demonstrated by microscopy data and time-course analysis of mitochondrial morphology.

claim: After 7 days of growth in YPD, approximately 85% of cells display small and immobile cortical mitochondrial vesicles.
source: With time, these fragments appeared shorter and shorter and after 7 days, the population was composed of ~85% of cells displaying small and immobile cortical mitochondrial vesicles (>50 per cell) that may be an ultimate form of tubule fragmentation.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the distribution of mitochondrial morphologies over time.

claim: After 7 days of growth in YPD, approximately 10% of cells exhibit 2 to 4 large globular mitochondria.
source: In addition, we found ~10% of cells exhibiting 2 to 4 large globular mitochondria and ~5% of cells in which we could not detected any Ilv3-RFP signal (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: After 7 days of growth in YPD, approximately 5% of cells show no detectable Ilv3-RFP signal.
source: In addition, we found ~10% of cells exhibiting 2 to 4 large globular mitochondria and ~5% of cells in which we could not detected any Ilv3-RFP signal (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Vesicular and globular mitochondria formation occurs independently of the mitochondria fission machinery.
source: Importantly, as in WT cells, after 7 days of growth in YPD, vesicular and globular mitochondria were observed in dnm1Δ, fis1Δ, caf4Δ, mdv1Δ and atg32Δ cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with deletion mutants of known fission machinery components.

claim: Vesicular and globular mitochondria formation occurs independently of selective mitophagy.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that upon proliferation cessation following glucose exhaustion, the mitochondrial network is drastically reshaped and thus, independently of both the mitochondria fission machinery (Labbé et al., 2014; Friedman and Nunnari, 2014) and selective mitophagy (Kanki et al., 2009; Okamoto et al., 2009).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with atg32Δ cells, which are defective in selective mitophagy.

claim: Mitochondrial DNA is detected in 89 ± 1% of 7 days old WT cells with globular mitochondria.
source: At the individual cell level, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) was detected in 89 ± 1% and 96% ± 1% of 7 days old WT cells with globular and vesicular mitochondria respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by DAPI staining data in Figure 1C.

claim: Mitochondrial DNA is detected in 96% ± 1% of 7 days old WT cells with vesicular mitochondria.
source: At the individual cell level, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) was detected in 89 ± 1% and 96% ± 1% of 7 days old WT cells with globular and vesicular mitochondria respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by DAPI staining data in Figure 1C.

claim: Vesicular mitochondria contain both respiratory chain enzymes and ATP synthase subunits.
source: However, while vesicular mitochondria contained both respiratory chain enzymes and ATP synthase subunits, some of OXPHOS proteins were not detected in 7-days-old cells with globular mitochondria (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy of cells expressing fluorescently tagged OXPHOS proteins.

claim: Some OXPHOS proteins are not detected in 7-days-old cells with globular mitochondria.
source: However, while vesicular mitochondria contained both respiratory chain enzymes and ATP synthase subunits, some of OXPHOS proteins were not detected in 7-days-old cells with globular mitochondria (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy showing absence of certain OXPHOS protein signals in cells with globular mitochondria.

claim: Cells with globular mitochondria are respiratory deficient.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that cells with globular mitochondria are respiratory deficient.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing that cells with globular mitochondria do not proliferate in respiratory medium (YPGE) and by ConA-FITC pulse-chase experiments.

claim: No cells with globular mitochondria were observed in cultures grown in rich medium containing respiratory carbon sources.
source: Accordingly, no cells with globular mitochondria were observed in cultures grown in rich medium containing respiratory carbon sources (glycerol/ethanol or lactate, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Unlike non-fluorescent cells, cells with vesicular or globular mitochondria are metabolically active.
source: Methylene blue staining revealed that unlike non-fluorescent cells, cells with vesicular or globular mitochondria were metabolically active (Figure 2A, Painting and Kirsop, 1990).
evidence: This is demonstrated by methylene blue staining, which identifies dead cells.

claim: More than 90% of 7-days-old cells that displayed vesicular mitochondria emitted a new bud within 6 hr after re-feeding.
source: Using this individual cell-tracking strategy, we found that more than 90% of the 7-days-old cells that displayed vesicular mitochondria emitted a new bud within 6 hr after re-feeding (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by individual cell tracking experiments on microscope pads.

claim: Cells with vesicular mitochondria are considered quiescent.
source: As such, they were considered as quiescent (Chi test value <10−26).
evidence: This is based on the operational definition of quiescence and statistical analysis of re-proliferation data.

claim: Upon quiescence exit, mitochondria vesicles rapidly fuse and reform short tubules before bud emergence.
source: Interestingly, upon quiescence exit, mitochondria vesicles rapidly fused and reformed short tubules before bud emergence (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-lapse microscopy of cells exiting quiescence.

claim: 98 ± 2% of cells with vesicular mitochondria are able to re-proliferate within 12 hr after re-feeding.
source: We found that 98 ± 2% of the cells with vesicular mitochondria were able to re-proliferate within 12 hr (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by extended individual cell tracking experiments.

claim: Approximately 90% of 7-days-old cells displaying globular mitochondria are unable to re-enter proliferation, even after 12 hr on microscope pad.
source: By contrast,~90% of the 7-days-old cells displaying globular mitochondria were unable to re-enter proliferation, even after 12 hr on microscope pad (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by individual cell tracking experiments.

claim: Cells with globular mitochondria that cannot re-proliferate are considered senescent.
source: These cells were thus considered as senescent (Chi test value <10−140).
evidence: This is based on the operational definition of senescence and statistical analysis.

claim: The percentage of cells with globular mitochondria able to re-proliferate progressively decreases over time.
source: As shown in Figure 2D, the percentage of cells with globular mitochondria able to re-proliferate within 6 hr on a pad progressively decreased.
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-course analysis of re-proliferation capacity.

claim: After 7 days, less than 10% of cells with globular mitochondria are able to re-proliferate.
source: After 7 days, less than 10% of these cells were able to re-proliferate, in agreement with Figure 2B.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: Respiratory deficient cells with globular mitochondria enter senescence in a non-synchronous manner.
source: These data indicate that respiratory deficient cells with globular mitochondria enter senescence, but in a non-synchronous manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the progressive decrease in re-proliferation capacity over time.

claim: Ethidium bromide treatment increases the percentage of cells with globular mitochondria.
source: This treatment induced an increase in the percentage of cells with globular mitochondria (Figure 2F), more than 90% of which being senescent after 7 days (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments using ethidium bromide to induce respiratory deficiency.

claim: More than 90% of cells with globular mitochondria induced by ethidium bromide treatment are senescent after 7 days.
source: This treatment induced an increase in the percentage of cells with globular mitochondria (Figure 2F), more than 90% of which being senescent after 7 days (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays of ethidium bromide-treated cells.

claim: Rho zero cells rearrange their mitochondrial network into 5 to 20 round and swollen mitochondria following carbon source exhaustion.
source: In parallel, we observed that following carbon source exhaustion, rho zero cells rearranged their mitochondrial network into 5 to 20 round and swollen mitochondria (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by microscopy of rho zero cells.

claim: 14 days old rho zero cells are alive but unable to re-proliferate on a microscope pad or to give rise to a progeny on plate.
source: After 14 days, these cells were alive but unable to re-proliferate on a microscope pad or to give rise to a progeny on plate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by viability staining and re-proliferation assays.

claim: 14 days old rho zero cells can be considered as senescent.
source: As such, 14 days old rho zero cells can be considered as senescent.
evidence: This is inferred from their inability to re-proliferate despite being alive.

claim: After 7 days of culture, mmm1Δ cells exhibit abnormally big mitochondria.
source: Accordingly, after 7 days of culture, mmm1Δ cells exhibited abnormally big mitochondria (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by microscopy of mmm1Δ cells.

claim: mmm1Δ cells are massively respiratory deficient (98 ± 4%).
source: As expected, mmm1Δ cells were massively respiratory deficient (98 ± 4%).
evidence: This is stated in the text and likely measured by plating on respiratory medium.

claim: After 16 days, most mmm1Δ cells appear senescent.
source: After 16 days, we found that most mmm1Δ cells appeared senescent (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by viability and colony forming assays.

claim: The inability to metabolize respiratory carbon sources correlates with the inability to maintain quiescence.
source: Taken together these experiments indicate that the inability to metabolize respiratory carbon sources correlates with the inability to maintain quiescence.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple experiments with respiratory deficient cells showing they become senescent.

claim: Upon respiratory carbon source exhaustion (glycerol/ethanol and lactate), no cell with globular mitochondria are observed.
source: As stated above, upon respiratory carbon source exhaustion (glycerol/ethanol and lactate), no cell with globular mitochondria were observed, the majority of the cells displaying a vesicular network and being quiescent.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Phosphate depletion leads to both globular and vesicular mitochondria formation.
source: Phosphate depletion, just as carbon depletion, led to both globular and vesicular mitochondria formation and more than 90% of the cells were able to form a colony.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Nitrogen exhaustion leads to massive mitophagy.
source: By contrast, as shown previously, nitrogen exhaustion led to massive mitophagy (Camougrand et al., 2008) and rapidly caused cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Nitrogen exhaustion rapidly causes cell death.
source: By contrast, as shown previously, nitrogen exhaustion led to massive mitophagy (Camougrand et al., 2008) and rapidly caused cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The mitochondrial network morphology can predict the fate of yeast cells facing chronological aging.
source: Hence, the mitochondrial network morphology can predict the fate of yeast cells facing chronological aging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation between mitochondrial morphology and cell re-proliferation capacity.

claim: The findings regarding mitochondrial morphology and cell fate are reproducible in both the W303 and the CEN-PK strain backgrounds.
source: In conclusion, the above data demonstrate that following carbon source exhaustion, the mitochondrial network organization correlates with individual cell fate: unstained cells are dead, cells with globular mitochondria appeared senescent and cells with vesicular mitochondria are quiescent (Figure 2H), these findings being reproducible in both the W303 and the CEN-PK strain backgrounds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1F–G.

claim: Dead cells are evenly distributed among the population regardless of cell volume.
source: First, methylene blue staining revealed that dead cells (black bars) were evenly distributed among the population, whatever the population age, indicating that cell volume and cell death are uncorrelated (Figure 3A, Chi-test value >0.1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by methylene blue staining and statistical analysis.

claim: Cell volume and cell death are uncorrelated.
source: First, methylene blue staining revealed that dead cells (black bars) were evenly distributed among the population, whatever the population age, indicating that cell volume and cell death are uncorrelated (Figure 3A, Chi-test value >0.1).
evidence: This is inferred from the even distribution of dead cells across different cell volumes.

claim: The 'small sub-population' is enriched in cells with globular mitochondria.
source: Second, we analyzed mitochondrial morphology and found that the 'small sub-population' was enriched in cells with globular mitochondria (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of mitochondrial morphology in cells of different volumes.

claim: There are more senescent cells among very small cells.
source: Thus, to some extent, we found more senescent cells among very small cells, in agreement with (Svenkrtova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of globular mitochondria in small cells and cited literature.

claim: Cell's ability to re-proliferate is not influenced by cell volume when considering exclusively cells with vesicular mitochondria.
source: Finally, when we considered exclusively cells with vesicular mitochondria, we found that cell's ability to re-proliferate was not influenced by the cell volume (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays of cells with vesicular mitochondria of different volumes.

claim: Cells with vesicular mitochondria enter quiescence whatever their volume.
source: These results demonstrate that cells with vesicular mitochondria enter quiescence whatever their volume.
evidence: This is concluded from the data showing no correlation between volume and re-proliferation capacity in cells with vesicular mitochondria.

claim: A cell's capacity to undergo chronological aging is unrelated to cell volume.
source: In agreement, using a collection of cell-size mutants, we found that a cell's capacity to undergo chronological aging was unrelated to cell volume (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with cell-size mutants.

claim: 4 hr after the diauxic shift, mother and daughter cells have a similar propensity to form globular mitochondria.
source: First, we found that 4 hr after the diauxic shift, mother and daughter cells have a similar propensity to form globular mitochondria (15 ± 6% and 11 ± 4% respectively (p-value=0.049)).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical analysis.

claim: 7-days-old mother and daughter cells with vesicular mitochondria have a similar ability of exiting quiescence within 6 hr.
source: Next, we observed that 7-days-old mother and daughter cells with vesicular mitochondria have a similar ability of exiting quiescence within 6 hr (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays comparing mother and daughter cells.

claim: The percentage of cells with globular or vesicular mitochondria is not significantly different between mother cell replicative age categories.
source: Interestingly, the percentage of cells with globular or vesicular mitochondria was not significantly different between mother cell replicative age categories (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of mitochondrial morphology in mother cells with different numbers of bud scars.

claim: Within mother cells with vesicular mitochondria, the replicative age does not influence cell re-proliferation capacities.
source: Finally and importantly, we found that within mother cells with vesicular mitochondria, the replicative age did not influence cell re-proliferation capacities (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays of mother cells with different numbers of bud scars.

claim: Cell's replicative age does not impinge on cell ability to face chronological aging, at least for cells that have undergone less than 15 divisions.
source: Thus, cell's replicative age does not impinges on cell ability to face chronological aging, at least for cells that have undergone less than 15 divisions.
evidence: This is concluded from the data showing no effect of replicative age on re-proliferation capacity for cells with up to 15 bud scars.

claim: The upper fraction from density gradient separation is enriched in cells with globular mitochondria (21 ± 4%).
source: Although, the upper fraction was enriched in cells with globular mitochondria (21 ± 4%) and dead cells (11 ± 1%), it contained ~70% of cells with vesicular mitochondria (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: The upper fraction from density gradient separation contains approximately 70% of cells with vesicular mitochondria.
source: Although, the upper fraction was enriched in cells with globular mitochondria (21 ± 4%) and dead cells (11 ± 1%), it contained ~70% of cells with vesicular mitochondria (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: The lower fraction from density gradient separation is composed of 96 ± 0% cells with vesicular mitochondria.
source: By comparison, the lower fraction was composed of 96 ± 0% and 1 ± 0% of cells with vesicular or globular mitochondria respectively and 3 ± 0% of dead cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: 96%, 96% and 95% of cells with vesicular mitochondria from the unfractionated population, the upper fraction and the lower fraction, respectively, are able to re-enter proliferation.
source: We found that 96%, 96% and 95% of cells with vesicular mitochondria from the unfractionated population, the upper fraction and the lower fraction, respectively, were able to re-enter proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays of cells from different density fractions.

claim: Cells with vesicular mitochondria can enter quiescence whatever their density.
source: These results demonstrate that cells with vesicular mitochondria can enter quiescence whatever their density.
evidence: This is concluded from the similar re-proliferation capacities of cells with vesicular mitochondria from different density fractions.

claim: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, mother cells are able to re-proliferate with the same efficiency as daughter cells whatever the fraction they belong to.
source: Moreover, in agreement with Figure 4A, among cells with vesicular mitochondria, mother cells were able to re-proliferate with the same efficiency than daughter cells whatever the fraction they belonged to (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays comparing mother and daughter cells from different density fractions.

claim: After 7 days in YPD, 85 ± 9% of cells display actin bodies (AB).
source: As expected from our previous studies, after 7 days in YPD, 85 ± 9% and 69 ± 1% of the cells displayed AB and PSG, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: After 7 days in YPD, 69 ± 1% of cells display proteasome storage granules (PSG).
source: As expected from our previous studies, after 7 days in YPD, 85 ± 9% and 69 ± 1% of the cells displayed AB and PSG, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: More than 90% of cells that display AB or PSG re-enter proliferation within 6 hr after re-feeding on a microscope pad.
source: More than 90% of the cells that displayed AB or PSG re-entered proliferation within 6 hr after re-feeding on a microscope pad (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by re-proliferation assays.

claim: AB or PSG formation and cell re-proliferation capacity are not independent.
source: Statistical analys indicated that AB or PSG formation and cell re-proliferation capacity were not independent (Chi-test value <10−13 and 10−53).
evidence: This is demonstrated by statistical analysis.

claim: The majority of 7-days-old WT cells with AB or PSG are quiescent.
source: Thus, the majority of 7-days-old WT cells with AB or PSG were quiescent.
evidence: This is inferred from the high re-proliferation capacity of cells with AB or PSG.

claim: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, 92% display AB.
source: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, we found that 92% and 65% displayed AB or PSG respectively, about 95% of which being capable to re-proliferate within 6 hr (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, 65% display PSG.
source: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, we found that 92% and 65% displayed AB or PSG respectively, about 95% of which being capable to re-proliferate within 6 hr (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: About 95% of cells with vesicular mitochondria and AB or PSG are capable to re-proliferate within 6 hr.
source: Among cells with vesicular mitochondria, we found that 92% and 65% displayed AB or PSG respectively, about 95% of which being capable to re-proliferate within 6 hr (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: A cell displaying AB and/or PSG and/or a vesicular mitochondrial network has at least 90% probability of being in a quiescent state after 7 days of culture in YPD.
source: These observations demonstrate that a cell displaying AB and/or PSG and/or a vesicular mitochondrial network has at least 90% probability of being in a quiescent state after 7 days of culture in YPD.
evidence: This is concluded from the high re-proliferation capacities of cells with these features.

claim: Among cells with globular mitochondria, 57% form AB.
source: Interestingly, among cells with globular mitochondria, 57% formed AB whereas none assembled PSG (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: None of the cells with globular mitochondria assemble PSG.
source: Interestingly, among cells with globular mitochondria, 57% formed AB whereas none assembled PSG (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: 5% of cells with AB display globular mitochondria.
source: Reciprocally, 5% of the cells with AB displayed globular mitochondria, but none of the cells with PSG displayed globular mitochondria (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: None of the cells with PSG display globular mitochondria.
source: Reciprocally, 5% of the cells with AB displayed globular mitochondria, but none of the cells with PSG displayed globular mitochondria (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: AB can assemble even if cells are unable to proliferate under respiratory conditions.
source: This strongly suggests that AB can assemble even if cells are unable to proliferate under respiratory conditions, while PSG can not.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cells with globular mitochondria (respiratory deficient) can form AB but not PSG.

claim: PSG cannot assemble if cells are unable to proliferate under respiratory conditions.
source: This strongly suggests that AB can assemble even if cells are unable to proliferate under respiratory conditions, while PSG can not.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cells with globular mitochondria (respiratory deficient) do not form PSG.

claim: 99 ± 1% of WT rho zero cells display AB.
source: Accordingly, 99 ± 1% of WT rho zero cells displayed AB (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), but none displayed bona fide PSG (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: None of the WT rho zero cells display bona fide PSG.
source: Accordingly, 99 ± 1% of WT rho zero cells displayed AB (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), but none displayed bona fide PSG (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: AB form in both quiescent and senescent cells.
source: Thus, AB form in both quiescent and senescent cells while PSG formation occurs only quiescent cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that AB are found in cells with both vesicular and globular mitochondria.

claim: PSG formation occurs only in quiescent cells.
source: Thus, AB form in both quiescent and senescent cells while PSG formation occurs only quiescent cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that PSG are only found in cells with vesicular mitochondria.

claim: Mitochondria play key roles in cellular aging.
source: Mitochondria play key roles in cellular aging (Sun et al., 2016; Kauppila et al., 2017; Sebastián et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to supporting literature.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, mitochondrial respiration dysfunctions severely affect cell's ability to face both replicative and chronological aging.
source: In S. cerevisiae, mitochondrial respiration dysfunctions severely affect cell's ability to face both replicative and chronological aging, (Fabrizio and Longo, 2003; Martinez et al., 2004; Trancíková et al., 2004; Bonawitz et al., 2006; Aerts et al., 2009; Ocampo et al., 2012; Beach et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Mitochondrial morphology defects have been observed in replicatively-old yeast mother cells.
source: Importantly, mitochondrial morphology defects have been observed in replicatively-old yeast mother cells (Scheckhuber et al., 2007; Veatch et al., 2009; McFaline-Figueroa et al., 2011; Hughes and Gottschling, 2012; Fehrmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to supporting literature.

claim: In proliferating yeast, mitochondria form a dynamic tubular meshwork.
source: In proliferating yeast, mitochondria form a dynamic tubular meshwork (Friedman and Nunnari, 2014) but intriguingly, in the early 1960's, Yotsuyanagi reported that upon proliferation cessation, mitochondria re-organize into peripherally-localized vesicles (Yotsuyanagi, 1962), a rearrangement also observed more recently (Stevens, 1981; Dürr et al., 2006; Sagot et al., 2006), but never investigated.
evidence: This is stated with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Yotsuyanagi reported that upon proliferation cessation, mitochondria re-organize into peripherally-localized vesicles.
source: In proliferating yeast, mitochondria form a dynamic tubular meshwork (Friedman and Nunnari, 2014) but intriguingly, in the early 1960's, Yotsuyanagi reported that upon proliferation cessation, mitochondria re-organize into peripherally-localized vesicles (Yotsuyanagi, 1962), a rearrangement also observed more recently (Stevens, 1981; Dürr et al., 2006; Sagot et al., 2006), but never investigated.
evidence: This is stated with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Quiescent cells are not all identical.
source: Overall, our findings reveal that not all quiescent cells are identical, yet quiescence establishment predominantly ensues upon the reorganization of specific cytoplasmic elements.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that quiescent cells display various physical and cellular features.

claim: Quiescence establishment predominantly ensues upon the reorganization of specific cytoplasmic elements.
source: Overall, our findings reveal that not all quiescent cells are identical, yet quiescence establishment predominantly ensues upon the reorganization of specific cytoplasmic elements.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that most quiescent cells display reorganization of mitochondria, actin, and proteasome.

claim: Quiescence is defined as a reversible, non-dividing cellular state.
source: First, it may enter quiescence, a reversible, non-dividing cellular state.
evidence: This is a standard definition stated in the introduction.

claim: Senescence is a state in which cells remain metabolically active but will never divide again.
source: Alternatively, a cell may enter senescence, a state in which cells remain metabolically active but will never divide again (Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007; Blagosklonny, 2011; O'Farrell, 2011; Valcourt et al., 2012; Cheung and Rando, 2013; Salama et al., 2014; Terzi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a standard definition stated with citations.

claim: The replicative age is the number of divisions a cell can potentially undergo before entering senescence.
source: The replicative age is the number of divisions a cell can potentially undergo before entering senescence (Mortimer and Johnston, 1959; Hayflick and Moorhead, 1961).
evidence: This is a standard definition stated with citations.

claim: The chronological age is the time a non-proliferating cell remains viable and capable of giving rise to a progeny.
source: The chronological age is the time a non-proliferating cell remains viable and capable of giving rise to a progeny (Fabrizio and Longo, 2003), quiescent cells being by definition the archetype of chronologically aging cells.
evidence: This is a standard definition stated with citation.

claim: Quiescent cells can currently only be identified a posteriori, after experimentally testing their capacity to re-proliferate.
source: This is a formidable technical challenge, particularly because quiescent cells can currently only be identified a posteriori, after experimentally testing their capacity to re-proliferate.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the field.

claim: When a yeast population exhausts one nutrient, it enters a so-called 'stationary phase'.
source: For example, when a yeast population exhausts one nutrient, it enters a so-called 'stationary phase' (Gray et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citation.

claim: The stationary phase population is heterogeneous and composed of quiescent, senescent and dead cells.
source: This population is heterogeneous and composed of quiescent, senescent and dead cells, the proportion of which evolves with time and differs depending on the nature of the exhausted nutrient (Davidson et al., 2011; Klosinska et al., 2011; Werner-Washburne et al., 2012; Laporte et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations.

claim: The Werner-Washburne laboratory pioneered studies utilizing a density gradient that separates the stationary phase population into two sub-fractions.
source: The Werner-Washburne laboratory has pioneered these studies utilizing a density gradient that separates the stationary phase population into two sub-fractions (Allen et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation.

claim: The Allen et al. study led to a Boolean concept in which only dense small daughter cells were considered as bona fide quiescent cells.
source: This study led to a Boolean concept in which only dense small daughter cells were considered as bona fide quiescent cells, while the light fraction, called non-quiescent, supposedly contained senescent and dead mother cells.
evidence: This is stated as a description of previous work.

claim: The Boolean model from Allen et al. is over-simplistic, as both sub-populations are highly heterogeneous and do contain quiescent cells.
source: Yet, as acknowledged later by the authors, this model is over-simplistic, as both sub-populations are highly heterogeneous and do contain quiescent cells (Aragon et al., 2008; Davidson et al., 2011; Werner-Washburne et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations acknowledging the limitations of the previous model.

claim: A sub-population of very small daughter cells (2–4 µm in diameter) contains mostly senescent or dead cells.
